title: The Educated Barbarian: Hagakure analysis (part. 22)
summary: Final episode of NH's Hagakure reading, covering humility of leaders, the balance of body and soul, mastering the self, working hard in youth, taking things one day at a time, and overcoming mental fears. He closes the bushido cycle (Book of Five Rings and Hagakure) and announces Marcus Aurelius' Meditations next.
claims: Leaders and elites exist to serve the people, not the reverse; a humble elite would see the collapse of the pyramid coming
Everyone needs a balance of body and soul; your calling may prioritize one, but you cannot abandon the other
Many people today let their body decay and mistake that abandonment for enlightenment, while pure gym-vanity types are equally wrong
The 'nice Jesus' doctrine turns Christians into doormats; real Christianity means standing up for what is right
No one can force you to be something you do not want to be; giving up your integrity means you have already lost what was worth protecting
Mastering your own body and mind is the only conquest that matters; once you change yourself, the world around you changes
Work hard while young and energetic and rest later; his immigrant parents taught him this
Youth is only the best part of life for people who wreck themselves; someone who takes care of themselves should still thrive at 40, 50, 60 and beyond
Two decades of hard work in your 20s and 30s can buy four decades of taking it easier with a good body
Stop viewing life in weekly or monthly blocks; focus on getting through one day, since the first step makes the mountain surmountable (blank-page stress)
Talented people need someone to confront them with their limits; without rivals in one sport he lost interest because he felt he had nothing to prove
Complaining about the state of the world is pointless because people make the era; become an expert and be a positive change instead of whining
Limiting factors are almost always mental; when he stopped telling himself what his body could do and let it show him, it was far more capable than he thought
Stay alert and grounded especially when things are going well, to avoid regret
Speak with few words and only say what you mean, so your words reflect your true mind
